courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Sustainable Development and Planning
courses.description:
This course critically examines the transformation of conventional urban planning and land development processes into sustainable, inclusive, and resilient systems. It is structured in two integrated parts:

Part I: Urban Development and Planning Frameworks
Students will explore the legal, administrative, and institutional structures that shape land development in Hong Kong and other global cities. Topics include zoning regulations, land use policy, environmental impact assessment, and governance mechanisms. Comparative case studies from cities such as Hong Kong, Singapore, Stockholm, New York, and Shenzhen will be used to highlight diverse planning models and their implications for sustainability.

Part II: Planning for Sustainable Urban Futures
Building on foundational knowledge, students will engage with international frameworks such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the New Urban Agenda to reimagine planning processes. Emphasis will be placed on climate-resilient infrastructure, adaptation planning, decarbonization, participatory planning, spatial justice, and circular urban systems that promote resource efficiency and regenerative design. Students will apply spatial planning tools (e.g. GIS, urban simulation, or data visualization) and policy analysis to propose sustainable interventions tailored to urban challenges in different contexts.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students will be able to:

* **Identify and explain** key legal, institutional, and environmental frameworks that shape urban planning and land development in Hong Kong and other global cities.
* **Apply and adapt** international sustainability frameworks, such as the SDGs and the New Urban Agenda, to local planning contexts through spatial analysis and policy evaluation.
* **Compare and contrast** diverse urban planning models and development strategies across global cities, evaluating their effectiveness in promoting sustainable outcomes.
* **Critically assess** the role of planning tools (e.g. GIS, urban simulation, data visualization) in diagnosing urban challenges and designing sustainable interventions.
* **Reflect on and evaluate** ethical dimensions of planning practice, including spatial justice, housing equity, and inclusive stakeholder engagement.
* **Synthesize and generalize** interdisciplinary concepts to formulate integrated planning strategies that address climate resilience, decarbonization, and circular urban systems.

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Territorial Spatial Planning Practice in China
courses.description: This course provides a practical introduction to China's Territorial Spatial Planning System, Case studies, and the latest planning policies and measures. The content covers: the evolution of the territorial spatial planning system; the basis, content, and case studies of macro, medium, and micro-level planning; special planning; spatial planning databases and cutting-edge practices, as well as the latest policies and issues (including "Beautiful China," low-carbon cities, sponge cities, resilient cities, smart city, high-speed rail and transit-oriented development, rural revitalization, urban renewal, and urban design).
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Planning Laws and Practice
courses.description:
There are various perspectives on understanding the legal system as it applies to town planning and practice in different contexts. In this course, the primary focus will be on development controls related to land use and the preparation of statutory town plans. It is also essential to adopt a multi-dimensional approach when handling planning matters.

The field of planning has evolved significantly over time. Today, three-dimensional spatial planning faces a range of emerging challenges, including broad issues such as nurturing biodiversity, reducing carbon emissions, and addressing socio-spatial and environmental justice, as well as localized concerns such as urban design, air ventilation, landscaping proposals, and traffic arrangements. Consequently, this specialized subject must remain current to equip professionals with the knowledge and skills needed to understand and effectively apply contemporary best planning practices.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Urban and Regional Economics
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and analytical frameworks of urban and regional economics. Students will learn how economic forces shape cities and regions through the behaviour of households, firms, and governments. Topics include location theory, land rent and land-use models, agglomeration economies, labour and housing markets, transport accessibility, and regional development. The course emphasises the application of microeconomic principles and quantitative tools to understand spatial patterns, evaluate policy interventions, and support evidence-based urban and regional planning.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:

* Understand basic microeconomic concepts as tools to explain the location choices of households and firms.

* Understand key theories of urban and regional economics, including location theory, agglomeration economies, land rent, and spatial equilibrium.

* Analyse the economic forces shaping cities and regions, such as labour markets, housing markets, transport accessibility, and innovation clusters.

* Apply quantitative and spatial analytical tools to evaluate urban economic patterns and policy interventions.

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Research Methods in Urban Planning
courses.description:
"Research Methods in Urban Planning" provides students with a comprehensive understanding of various qualitative and quantitative research techniques essential for analyzing, designing, and evaluating urban environments. Through critical examination of data collection, analysis methods, and case studies, students will develop the skills to conduct rigorous and evidence-based research tailored to urban planning challenges. Emphasis will be placed on integrating theoretical frameworks with practical applications to address complex urban issues.

Students will also learn to critically assess the strengths and limitations of different research methodologies and ethical considerations relevant to urban planning related research. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to design and implement independent research projects, effectively communicate findings, and contribute to informed policy-making and planning practice.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
courses.learning_outcomes:
* Critically evaluate a broad range of qualitative and quantitative research methods relevant to urban planning.
* Design and develop rigorous research proposals that address complex urban planning issues using appropriate methodologies.
* Apply advanced data collection and analysis techniques to investigate urban phenomena and interpret findings within planning contexts.
* Integrate theoretical frameworks with empirical research to formulate evidence-based urban planning strategies and solutions.
* Assess ethical considerations and challenges in urban planning research and ensure adherence to professional standards.
* Communicate research outcomes effectively to diverse audiences, including policymakers, practitioners, and academic peers.

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Spatial Planning Studio I
courses.description: This studio aims to equip students with basic spatial planning and design skills. Students will learn the spatial planning process from baseline review to formulation of spatial planning framework and development proposals. Various planning skills, including community auditing, public engagement methods, digital techniques, visualization, GIS, place-making and design thinking approaches will be introduced with real-life examples in planning practice. Students will be provided with opportunities to practise various skills to understand their application in different spatial contexts.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:

* develop proficiency in mastering various spatial planning and design skills
* understand the application of spatial planning skills in real-world planning practice, and
* gain teamwork experience which fosters critical thinking skills and collaborative learning

courses.subject: SDUP
courses.title: Spatial Planning Studio II
courses.description: This studio encourages students to use their skills to conduct spatial planning and design exercises at different geographical levels, ranging from regional development strategy to community and neighbourhood planning. Students will be provided with opportunities to engage different stakeholders to develop a sustainable planning strategy which integrates social inclusion, economic vitality and environmental protection.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Sustainable Urban Planning
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:

* apply spatial planning skills to develop planning and development strategies at the community and regional levels,
* Understand the complex relationships between spatial planning and enhancing environmental, economic and social sustainability
* engage different stakeholders and balance their interests in the planning process, and
* gain teamwork experience which fosters critical thinking skills and collaborative learning
